summary: SF_STUCCO_EXT_NC_v1 draft artifacts pass all critical doctrine checks with 2 major issues requiring acknowledgment. Fourth exterior spec — follows masonry, fiber cement, and engineered wood siding siblings. 41 tasks thread correctly between sop_modules.json and production.json (29 binary, 10 qt_scaled, 2 qt_conditional) with zero orphaned tasks, zero UOM mismatches, and zero classification mismatches. All PaintScope keys use PS_EXT_* namespace. Single substrate state SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY in resolution.json (no factory-primed stucco exists). All 5 protection zones use ext_* prefix. No interior keys, states, or zones present. Key stucco-specific features: two substrate types (traditional_stucco/EIFS) with HARD CONSTRAINT elastomeric PROHIBITED on EIFS (COMPAT-STCO-002), alkali-resistant primer mandatory on traditional stucco, standard acrylic primer for EIFS, spray_backroll coupling enforced with crew_size=2 on all 6 spray_backroll tasks, oil-based products prohibited (COMPAT-STCO-001), crack >1/8 inch hard stop (COMPAT-STCO-008), EIFS LRV >20 constraint (COMPAT-STCO-003), EIFS insurance verification gate present, texture profile drives DUAL multiplier on labor AND material. 2 major issues found: (1) materials.json uses SS_EXT_BARE_STUCCO and SS_EXT_BARE_EIFS substrate states instead of the SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY declared in resolution.json and research.json — cross-file threading inconsistency; (2) materials.json texture multiplier values (sand=1.30, lace=1.85, dash=3.25) diverge significantly from resolution.json values (sand=1.25, lace=1.50, dash=2.00) — the materials values appear to be field-derived from coverage ratio calculations while resolution values appear to be rounded/simplified estimates. No critical blockers.

issues.description: materials.json declares substrate_states as SS_EXT_BARE_STUCCO (on SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI) and SS_EXT_BARE_EIFS (on SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ACRYLIC). Resolution.json and research.json consistently declare the single NC substrate state as SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY for both substrate types. sop_modules.json also correctly references SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY in primer task state_routing. The materials.json substrate_states field is inconsistent with the upstream resolution — it invented two substrate state IDs that are not in the controlled enum registry.
issues.resolution: Materials.json substrate_states should be corrected to SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY on both primer systems, matching resolution.json. The substrate_type dimension (traditional_stucco vs EIFS) already correctly gates primer selection via applies_when — the substrate_state is the same for both (bare cementitious/uncoated). If separate substrate states are desired, they must be proposed through the resolution and added to controlled_enums.

issues.description: Resolution.json FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE declares texture multiplier values as smooth=1.00, sand=1.25, lace=1.50, dash=2.00. Materials.json coverage_profiles declare surface_texture_modifier values that diverge: COV_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI uses sand=1.30, lace=1.85, dash=3.25; COV_STCO_FINISH_ACRYLIC uses sand=1.30, lace=1.85, dash=2.50; COV_STCO_FINISH_ELASTOMERIC uses sand=1.30, lace=1.85, dash=2.50. The materials values cite derivation from SF/gal coverage ratios (325/250=1.30, 325/175=1.86, 325/100=3.25) while resolution values appear to be simplified round numbers. Production.json references FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE with the resolution values (1.00/1.25/1.50/2.00) for labor rates.
issues.resolution: Acknowledged — the divergence is deliberate design. Resolution.json defines the LABOR rate multiplier (conservative, rounded). Materials.json defines the MATERIAL consumption multiplier (field-derived from coverage ratios, necessarily different because material absorption scales non-linearly with texture depth while labor scales more linearly). The dual-pathway nature of the texture modifier means labor and material multipliers are expected to differ. However, the naming collision is confusing — materials.json uses surface_texture_modifier while production.json uses FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE, and the values are different. Recommend documenting this dual-pathway explicitly in spec.json when created.

issues.description: Production.json declares environmental factor modifiers (FAC_EXT_WIND, FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE, FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP) as process constraint documentation, consistent with the masonry sibling pattern. Research.json explicitly states environmental conditions are EXCLUDED from estimation (RC-002). These modifiers serve as scheduling constraints with BLOCKED states rather than estimation modifiers.
issues.resolution: Acknowledged — consistent with masonry sibling pattern (masonry QA-002). Environmental modifiers document process constraints and blocking conditions. No change needed.

issues.description: Research.json RC-004 explicitly states no substrate condition modifier (FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION) is needed because this is a new construction spec with controlled substrate conditions. Production.json correctly omits this modifier. However, the critic agent exterior dispatch block lists FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION as a check item (EXT-5). This is a correct omission for NC specs.
issues.resolution: Acknowledged — FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION is correctly excluded per research RC-004. NC stucco arrives in known condition; substrate condition variability is a repaint concern only.

doctrine_checks.details: All 41 task_ids in sop_modules.json have matching entries in production.json. No orphaned tasks in either direction. Verified programmatically. Count by module: SETUP=6, PREP=12, PRIME=5, FINISH_1=5, INTERSTAGE=3, FINISH_2=5, FINAL_INSPECT=2, CLEANUP=3.

All task_classification values match between files. 10 qt_scaled tasks (PRESSURE_WASH, EIFS_WASH, MILDEW_TREAT, EFFLORESCENCE_TREAT, CRACK_PATCH, SURFACE_PATCH, CAULK_JOINTS, INSPECT_INTERCOAT, FINAL_INSPECT, TOUCHUP) have qt_rates in production.json. 2 qt_conditional tasks (SAND_INTERCOAT, DUST_INTERCOAT) have appears_in_tiers restrictions. 29 binary tasks use flat rate_per_hour or fixed_time_minutes.

Application method gating consistent between files: spray_backroll tasks gate on [spray_backroll], roll on [roll, spray_backroll], brush on [brush]. Substrate_type gating consistent: alkali primer tasks on [traditional_stucco], acrylic primer tasks on [EIFS], elastomeric finish tasks on [traditional_stucco] with coating_system [elastomeric], acrylic finish tasks on coating_system [acrylic]. EIFS knock test gates on [EIFS]. Efflorescence treatment gates on [traditional_stucco]. Cure verification gates on [traditional_stucco].

All task UOMs match between sop_modules.json and production.json. Zero mismatches verified programmatically. SF-based: 22 tasks (prime, finish, wash, patch, inspect, touchup, sand, dust). LF-based: 3 tasks (landscape protect, crack patch, caulk joints). EA-based: 2 tasks (fixture mask, HVAC cover). FIXED: 14 tasks (spray setup, crack assess, EIFS knock test, moisture test, cure verify, EIFS insurance verify, inspect intercoat, final inspect, protect teardown, tool clean, waste dispose).
All 41 task IDs use TSK_STCO_ prefix consistently. No collisions with existing prefixes (SDNG, FCSD, MSRY, etc.). STCO is unique per resolution.json collision check.
All 8 module IDs use MOD_STCO_ prefix: SETUP, PREP, PRIME, FINISH_1, INTERSTAGE, FINISH_2, FINAL_INSPECT, CLEANUP.

All 5 material system IDs match between resolution.json and materials.json: SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI, SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ACRYLIC, SYS_EXT_STCO_FINISH_ACRYLIC_STD, SYS_EXT_STCO_FINISH_ACRYLIC_PREM, SYS_EXT_STCO_FINISH_ELASTOMERIC. Naming follows SYS_EXT_STCO_ pattern per resolution.
All 4 coverage profile IDs match between resolution.json and materials.json: COV_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI, COV_STCO_PRIMER_ACRYLIC, COV_STCO_FINISH_ACRYLIC, COV_STCO_FINISH_ELASTOMERIC.

All paintscope_key references use PS_EXT_* namespace. 12 PS keys declared in resolution.json: PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.STUCCO_FIELD, PS_EXT_META.EA.ELEVATIONS_TOTAL, PS_EXT_META.ENUM.ACCESS_TYPE, PS_EXT_META.FLAG.NEW_CONSTRUCTION, PS_EXT_META.ENUM.SUBSTRATE_TYPE_STUCCO, PS_EXT_META.ENUM.TEXTURE_PROFILE_STUCCO, PS_EXT_META.ENUM.COATING_SYSTEM_STUCCO, PS_EXT_META.FLAG.EIFS_INSURANCE_VERIFIED, PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER, PS_EXT_PROTECT_SF.HARDSCAPE_WALK, PS_EXT_PROTECT_SF.HARDSCAPE_PATIO, PS_EXT_PROTECT_EA.LIGHT_FIXTURE, PS_EXT_PROTECT_EA.HVAC_UNIT. No interior keys found.

Resolution.json, research.json, and sop_modules.json consistently use SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY. Output states: SS_EXT_PAINTED_FLAT, SS_EXT_PAINTED_SATIN. All use SS_EXT_* prefix. No SS_INT_* IDs. WARNING: materials.json uses SS_EXT_BARE_STUCCO and SS_EXT_BARE_EIFS which are not declared in resolution.json or controlled_enums. See QA-001.

All 5 protection zones use ext_* prefix: ext_landscape_perimeter, ext_hardscape_walk, ext_hardscape_patio, ext_light_fixture, ext_hvac_unit. No interior zone IDs. Window/door zones correctly excluded per cross-spec boundary.

Access_type declared as site_condition_rule with height modifier values (ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50). Wind, sun_exposure, and surface_temp referenced as environmental modifiers in production.json with BLOCKED states for extreme conditions. Environmental conditions excluded from estimation per RC-002.

FAC_EXT_ACCESS reused from siding/masonry specs. FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE declared (smooth=1.00, sand=1.25, lace=1.50, dash=2.00). FAC_STCO_SUBSTRATE_TYPE declared (traditional_stucco=1.00, EIFS=0.90). FAC_QT declared (QT2=0.85, QT3=1.00, QT4=1.20). FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION correctly omitted per RC-004 (NC spec). No interior modifiers present.

All modifiers use division formula: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Stacking cap 4.0x declared. 6 stacking examples provided. Maximum combination (dash 2.00 x traditional 1.00 x scaffold 1.60 x QT4 1.20 = 3.84x) is under 4.0x cap. Worst case effective rate: 23 SF/hr per 2-person crew on elastomeric spray_backroll finish — extremely slow but viable for estimation.

COMPAT-STCO-002 explicitly blocks elastomeric on EIFS with severity critical. SYS_EXT_STCO_FINISH_ELASTOMERIC applies_when gates on substrate_type [traditional_stucco] only. Elastomeric finish tasks gate on coating_system [elastomeric] which is only valid when substrate_type = traditional_stucco. Research RF-003 documents catastrophic moisture entrapment risk. Multiple redundant safeguards prevent EIFS + elastomeric combination.

COMPAT-STCO-001 explicitly prohibits oil-based and alkyd products on all stucco substrates. Severity: critical. All material systems in materials.json are water-based (acrylic latex, elastomeric, acrylic primer). Traditional stucco: alkaline saponification risk. EIFS: chemical incompatibility with acrylic system and EPS dissolution risk.

6 spray_backroll tasks present: TSK_STCO_PRIME_ALKALI_SPRAY_BACKROLL, TSK_STCO_PRIME_ACRYLIC_SPRAY_BACKROLL, TSK_STCO_FINISH_ACRYLIC_SPRAY_BACKROLL_1, TSK_STCO_FINISH_ELASTO_SPRAY_BACKROLL_1, TSK_STCO_FINISH_ACRYLIC_SPRAY_BACKROLL_2, TSK_STCO_FINISH_ELASTO_SPRAY_BACKROLL_2. All have crew_size=2 in production.json. All gate on application_method [spray_backroll]. COMPAT-STCO-006 enforces spray = auto-add backroll. Spray-only is PROHIBITED per Application Methods Doctrine Part A section 6.

doctrine_checks.check: STCO-4: Crack Assessment FIRST in Prep
doctrine_checks.details: TSK_STCO_CRACK_ASSESS is the first task in MOD_STCO_PREP (line 137 in sop_modules.json). Cracks >1/8 inch = HARD STOP per COMPAT-STCO-008. Structural assessment required before any coating work. Correct sequencing.

COMPAT-STCO-003 requires LRV >20 (preferably >50) for EIFS colors. Low LRV causes excessive solar heat absorption leading to EPS expansion/contraction and system delamination. Documented as a specification verification step.

TSK_STCO_EIFS_INSURANCE_VERIFY present in MOD_STCO_PREP. Gates on substrate_type [EIFS]. FIXED time task (administrative). PS_EXT_META.FLAG.EIFS_INSURANCE_VERIFIED workflow flag declared. CGL policy exclusion risk documented.

doctrine_checks.check: STCO-7: Alkali-Resistant Primer Mandatory on Traditional Stucco
doctrine_checks.details: SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI applies_when substrate_type [traditional_stucco]. COMPAT-STCO-004 enforces mandatory alkali-resistant primer. Standard acrylic primer explicitly noted as unsuitable (pH <9 design vs pH 12-14 on new stucco). All quality tiers require alkali-resistant primer.

TSK_STCO_PROTECT_LANDSCAPE uses UOM=LF in both sop_modules.json and production.json. Input key IN_LF_EXT_PROTECT_LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER maps to PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER. Consistent with RC-003 and masonry sibling pattern.

5 protection zones declared in resolution.json: ext_landscape_perimeter, ext_hardscape_walk, ext_hardscape_patio, ext_light_fixture, ext_hvac_unit. All referenced in sop_modules.json setup tasks with corresponding teardown in cleanup module.

5 adjacent surfaces declared in research.json adjacency_analysis: ext_trim_window_casing, ext_trim_door_casing, soffit_field, foundation_wall, ext_trim_frieze. No edge work within this spec — all adjacent surfaces are separate spec scopes.

3 active round configurations in sop_modules.json: ROUND_STCO_PRIME_2FINISH (QT3/QT4 both substrates), ROUND_STCO_PRIME_1FINISH (QT2 both substrates), ROUND_STCO_PRIME_2FINISH_ELASTO (traditional stucco QT3/QT4 elastomeric). Resolution also proposed ROUND_STCO_PRIME_1FINISH_ELASTO as PLACEHOLDER (never activates — elastomeric excluded at QT2). Covers all valid substrate_type x quality_tier x coating_system combinations.

Module phase sequence: setup (SETUP) -> prep (PREP) -> prime (PRIME) -> finish (FINISH_1) -> interstage (INTERSTAGE) -> finish (FINISH_2) -> cleanup (FINAL_INSPECT, CLEANUP). Phase ordering follows structural_keys convention. No 'protect' or 'protection' phase values.

13 input declarations in resolution.json with paintscope_key mappings: 1 surface input (IN_SF_STUCCO_WALL), 3 meta inputs (IN_EA_ELEVATIONS, IN_ENUM_ACCESS_TYPE, IN_BOOL_NEW_CONSTRUCTION), 3 stucco config inputs (IN_ENUM_SUBSTRATE_TYPE_STUCCO, IN_ENUM_TEXTURE_PROFILE_STUCCO, IN_ENUM_COATING_SYSTEM_STUCCO), 1 workflow flag (IN_BOOL_EIFS_INSURANCE_VERIFIED), 5 protection inputs. All consumed by sop_modules.json or production.json.

All enums comply with project conventions: CON_ prefix (not CONS_), task_classification (not task_class), severity uses critical/major/minor, phase values from approved set (no 'protect' or 'protection' phase), all units uppercase (EA, SF, LF, FIXED, TUBE, ROLL, GAL), consumable_category from approved set (applicator, protection, prep, cleanup, fill_material, tool), zone uses ext_* prefix, sheen single values only (flat, satin — no compound sheens).

exterior_validation_summary.interior_contamination: none — no interior keys, states, or zones found
key_departures_from_masonry_sibling: Two substrate types (traditional_stucco/EIFS) vs masonry's 5 (brick/CMU/concrete/limestone + smooth/rough split) — fewer subtypes but with fundamentally different coating constraints
EIFS = acrylic ONLY hard constraint — masonry has no equivalent material prohibition by substrate type
No block filler module — stucco has no voids to fill (unlike CMU masonry). 8 modules vs masonry's 9
Texture profile as DUAL multiplier on labor AND material — masonry uses substrate_type as single-pathway labor modifier only
Two separate primer paths (alkali-resistant for traditional, acrylic for EIFS) vs masonry's single alkali-resistant primer for all substrates
EIFS insurance verification gate — unique to stucco, no equivalent in masonry
EIFS knock test — unique to stucco, delamination detection not applicable to masonry
Pressure wash branched by substrate type (1500-3000 PSI traditional vs <500 PSI EIFS) — masonry uses uniform pressure settings
41 total tasks vs masonry's 31 — more tasks due to substrate-branched primer and finish paths
3 active round configurations vs masonry's 4 — no block filler dimension but elastomeric round added
Maximum modifier stacking 3.84x vs masonry's 3.744x — stucco texture modifier (2.00x dash) drives higher stack

modifier_stacking_validation.worst_case_scenario: Dash texture (2.00) x traditional stucco (1.00) x scaffold (1.60) x QT4 (1.20) = 3.84x
modifier_stacking_validation.worst_case_effective_rate: 23 SF/hr per 2-person crew on elastomeric spray_backroll finish — extremely slow but viable for fixed-price estimation

material_system_validation.substrate_state_inconsistency: materials.json uses SS_EXT_BARE_STUCCO/SS_EXT_BARE_EIFS vs resolution SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY — see QA-001
